items.reviewText: There are jokes about ADHD adults racking up piles of under-used planners without ever getting more organized, but this one actually seemed to help. There are pages specific to the overview of a whole week, then individual day pages. There is a miniature daily calendar on... There are jokes about ADHD adults racking up piles of under-used planners without ever getting more organized, but this one actually seemed to help. There are pages specific to the overview of a whole week, then individual day pages. There is a miniature daily calendar on the page, that allows you to see how your tasks fit into the day. Just having the expectation that you will sit down and look at the whole day and how it all fits together tends to improve organization. There are task lists for the most immediate tasks, those of secondary importance, and a list of things to delegate. I have limited opportunity to delegate in my job, so I used that column for things to do once I got home from work. When a task didn’t get done, I carried it forward to the next day, which was a motivator—it became a frustration when a task was forwarded over and over, and eventually I wanted it to be done so I didn’t have to carry it forward. Each day has a set of icons at the top which are not assigned designations, so you can choose what to make them about. Will you circle what you plan to do? Will you only circle what you did accomplish? I often underlined things that were my intention, and completed the circle if I completed the task. You could also cross out an icon to say that you are not going to engage in that task, that day, just to alleviate any tension around it. There are ‘self-awareness’ elements on each page including the mood and energy level for the day. I love that it’s not trying to do too much. Other planners try to help you ‘fix’ your entire life/mindset all in 3-6 months, and I think that’s where ADHD-ers get lost. If you’re at the advanced stage of examining and organizing your life, seek out something more complex, but if you’re just trying to figure out how to make daily life fit together without dropping stuff through the cracks, I recommend starting here, and maybe graduating later to a ‘whole-life-makeover’ type organizer. [True confession—I bought one of the more advanced ones, and I think I may shelve it and go back to this one for a while longer].

items.reviewText: I was extremely excited to find this notebook. I thought it would be just what I needed to help organize my racing thoughts/ideas, business and personal appointments, notes, task lists, etc., all in one convenient place to eliminate multiple tracking methods to write in but... I was extremely excited to find this notebook. I thought it would be just what I needed to help organize my racing thoughts/ideas, business and personal appointments, notes, task lists, etc., all in one convenient place to eliminate multiple tracking methods to write in but it's not the solution for me. Likes: 1) This NB is very sturdy and well made. 2) It's a manageable size, which is a plus because you could easily carry it in a purse, workbag, etc., to jot down everything throughout the day to stay organized and on track. Dislikes: 1) Unfortunately, what I dislike is the lack of color. All the pages look like a newspaper and are void of any character. That would be fine if I carried an extensive array of colored pens, markers, and highlighters to jazz it up and took time to make the categories stand out, but that's not happening. The lack of color complaint is 100% on me because I didn't pay attention to the product pics well enough before ordering it to notice the repetitive black/white pages with zero colors. For whatever reason, my attention deficit brain works better with visual stimulation. Others reading my review may not have that issue. 2) Too many categories are broken out on one page for the overall week, followed by individual pages for each weekday that include numerous categories. I thought that would be positive and helpful, but although each category is labeled well and separated fine, these sections don’t stand out the way I need to be beneficial. It’s become overwhelming with “so much” versus simplifying my day. Again, that is another me problem that not everyone reading this review will experience. In providing my review, I also realized that I’m disappointed with this item because I need monthly calendars in whatever daily planner I use. I am just hoping that one day a product will be created where my spastic brain can have a single planner to keep business and personal in one perfect place. To sum it up, I'm still searching for my ideal planner. However, these are my opinions, and your preferences may differ entirely. This product might be perfect for you. Cheers!

items.reviewText: First this is a really cute planner and I love the stickers. It has undated pages which is great for add minds. But- the first few pages include what I can only describe as “what people without adhd think adhd is”, I’m not really sure why it’s included. It’s like explaining the medical description of ADHD which i guess some people will agree with but this is so different for different people. No one experiences the text book definitions of adhd. Like for me, hearing “hey squirrel” is not really helpful. It’s not a fun joke to be constantly distracted and it’s not just because stuff is shiny. So a little insulting. And the doodle pages are nice but why are there so many pages of squirrels? After coloring one page of squirrels I’m bored by having to repeat that same picture. So Idk. I’ll use the actual planner pages because those are great. The extra stuff? Not so much.

items.reviewTitle: A little odd.... I don't like the denying that ADHD is a disability.
items.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on November 29, 2024
items.reviewText: I don't love that some of it treats ADHD the way it does, kind of making it a joke or meme rather than actually trying to be helpful and sympathetic. "Oh look, a squirrel!" is such an old joke now. Sure, I love squirrels and I think they're cute, but I think it's a little strange to theme it around that so much. The daily pages are nice, but for me they often end up mostly blank. I like the weekly and monthly review pages though, being able to point out noteworthy things is something I haven't really done this way before. I HATE the quote they used " ADHD isn't a disability, it's a different ability" - no, it IS a disability. It's not bad to have a disability! Stop placing stigma on being disabled. Disabled people can be capable, and some disabled people have brains that work differently from neurotypicals - that's cool, but it is still a disability with the world we live in. Deciding it's not a disability also makes it harder for people to get help they need and makes people feel bad when they're not able to do things the way "normal" people do. Acknowledging it as a disability and respecting it gives resources and support and explains why someone with ADHD may need help, and that it's not a personal failing the way many people think it is. It is not your fault if you have ADHD and struggle with certain things - it's a disability, and you deserve understanding and kindness, not denial. Also, ADHD is considered a disability by the ADA and various other organizations, so it's just straight out lying to you. I find this offensive and I do not support this messaging. Anyway... The paper is pretty thin, I can see through it just with the ink printed on it, so you have to be careful with what you use to write with and how hard you push on the paper. It could be good to use a few spare sheets of paper under the page you're writing on to prevent ink bleeding and damaging the other pages if you tend to press somewhat hard. The squirrel coloring pages all look similar and super childish - which isn't necessarily bad, but more variety would be better than having them all basically be the same... It's not all bad, I like that there's little ribbon bookmarks and the pages generally do look nice. I think it could work really well for some people (maybe for people who enjoy the ADHD squirrel joke and hate the idea of having a disability.......). Overall, do i recommend this item? No, I don't. I think a few simple changes could make it significantly better though, so I hope they consider that. If they removed disability denial and the squirrel jokes, and made the pages a little thicker, I think it could be a decent product.

items.reviewText: Such a beautiful and well organized planner to keep you creative all year round. I loved the quality of the book and how well they mapped out the planning section. I snagged this for my husband as he really needed one. He has a hard time keeping track of certain things. This planner is the perfect solution for him. He also has so much going on in his brain, it gets clouded. I really liked the brain dump section as well for this exact purpose. Helps him jot down small thoughts or even doodles. They also gave you inspirational note cards, which I loved. They have a monthly calendar in between the 30 days of planning. Along with beautiful words of wisdom/affirmations. I do recommend!

items.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on October 21, 2024
items.reviewText: This is my second attempt at leaving a review. This is a really nice planner. Good, solid, hardcover to prevent bending of pages or even the cover when tucked into a backpack. There is a good variety of pages that should work for however you most like to use your planner (I love checkboxes, for instance). Two ribbon book marks allow for quick access to both the current day's plans and important notes. This comes with a few small extras that I didn't need, but I know some people like these things. This is larger than my preferred planner size (I prefer A5 size which is a little smaller than this).

So far, that's not a solution for me, even if I do enjoy it and find it periodically helpful.
